big_idea: The $100 bill is BROWN. We make amounts up to $200 with bills and coins.
learning_intention: We are learning to make amounts up to $200.
student_learning_goal: I can make amounts up to $200.
success_criteria: I can MAKE $100 with smaller bills.
I can EXPLAIN equivalent amounts to $200.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tappy + Lou — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Bill Cards including $100 (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Loonie Lou: Friends — meet the BROWN $100 bill! Today we make amounts up to $200! Tappy opens: 'ONE HUNDRED — many WAYS!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Lou puppet with bills. 'Money friends — yesterday we did $25, $35. Today bigger — UP TO $200!'

Reveal $100. 'BROWN colour. ROBERT BORDEN on front. = $100.00!'

Demo 3 ways for $100:
- WAY 1: 1 HUNDRED bill alone.
- WAY 2: 5 TWENTIES (5 × 20 = $100).
- WAY 3: 2 FIFTIES (2 × 50 = $100).

'Lou says — $100 bill = 5 twenties = 2 fifties!'

Demo 3 ways for $150:
- WAY 1: 1 HUNDRED + 1 FIFTY.
- WAY 2: 1 HUNDRED + 2 TWENTIES + 1 TEN.
- WAY 3: 7 TWENTIES + 1 TEN ($140 + $10 = $150).

Class verifies each total.

'Lou says — bigger amounts = bigger bills helpful!'

Define. 'CANADIAN DOLLAR (CAD) = our money. Different from US dollar.'

Now each pair gets Bill + Coin Cards. Target: $150. Find 2 ways.

'Lou says — start with $100, then add!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Bill + Coin Cards. Target: $150. Find 2 ways.

STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share $100 combos. Class: 'Whose used FEWEST bills? Whose used MOST denominations? All $100?' Cite Sowder (1992) unitizing — the math AMOUNT is constant, the UNITS chosen are flexible.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tappy: 'Same TOTAL, different DENOMINATIONS. The unit is YOUR choice.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to bill stations. NO-MATERIALS PATH: children use FINGERS as bills (open hand = $50 bill, closed fist = $100 bill, thumbs-up = $20).

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: identifies $100; makes $150; verifies; records; finds 2.

discussion_prompts: What is the maximum amount this year?
consolidation.exit_routine: Tappy's hundred refrain — 'ONE HUNDRED — many WAYS! Each combo = one BENJAMIN!' Then unit close: 'SAME AMOUNT, MANY WAYS!' Each child writes one $100 combo on a sticky.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says $100 = 100 loonies — repairing the impractical-combo trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On $100 composition, the trap is unit-coin perseveration / denomination-equivalence failure (Carraher & Schliemann on currency cognition; Sowder 1992 on quantitative units): child tries to reach $100 with $5 bills only because $5 is comfortable, or assumes the $100 bill cannot be decomposed at all.

Yesterday Lesson 3 mixed bills + coins for $35. Today scales to $100 with denomination flexibility. Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Lou asks — could you use a BILL instead?'

Probe. 'There's a $100 BILL! 1 piece = $100. Way easier.'

Generalise. 'Lou says — we have BILLS for big amounts. Use them!'

If still all coins: 'Try $100 bill. Or 2 fifties. Faster than 100 coins.'
common_misconceptions: Always use coins. (Repair: bills for big.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child uses $5 bills only ($5 × 20 = $100): force a $50 + $50 alternative; child names two equivalent combos.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child cannot decompose $100: physical demo with a $100 bill replica + ten $10 bills; show 'one $100 = ten $10s.'
DIAGNOSTIC C — child uses bills only: require ONE quarter somewhere in their $100 combo (e.g., $99.75 + 1 quarter).
